verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              भीमसेनस्ततः कृष्णमुवाच यदुनन्दनम्। बुद्धिमास्थाय विपुलां जरासन्धवधोप्सया॥१॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said Thereupon Bhimsena, his mind firmly set on the desire of killing Jarasandha, thus spoke to the descendant of Yadu, Krishna, "O Krishna, O best of the Yadu race, this wretch is still before me with girded loins and with sufficient strength. He should not be excused by me,”

verses.sanskrit: नायं पापो मया कृष्ण युक्तः स्यादनुरोधितुम्। प्रायेण यदुशार्दूल बद्धकक्षेण वाससा॥२॥
एवमुक्तस्ततः कृष्णः प्रत्युवाच वृकोदरम्। त्वरयन्पुरुषव्याघ्रो जरासन्धवधेप्सया॥३॥
verses.english: Having been thus addressed, the high minded Krishna, well-skilled in speech, thus replied to him in a calm and grave voice.

verses.sanskrit: यत्ते दैवं परं सत्वं यच्च ते मातरिश्वनः। बलं भीम जरासन्धे दर्शयाशु तदद्य वै॥४॥
verses.english: Having been thus addressed, Krishna, that best of men, with the desire of seeing soon an end of Jarasandha, thus replied to Vrikodara (Bhima), “O Bhima, the strength that you have derived from the celestials, the might that you have obtained from Maruta, display them today towards Jarasandha."

verses.sanskrit: एवमुक्तस्तदा भीमो जरासन्धमरिन्दमः। उत्क्षिप्य भ्रामयामास बलवन्तं महाबलः॥५॥
verses.english: Having been thus addressed, that chastiser of foes, that greatly strong (hero), Bhima, raised up the strong Jarasandha and whirled him on high.

verses.sanskrit: भ्रामयित्वा शतगुणं जानुभ्यां भरतर्षभ। बभञ्ज पृष्ठं सङ्क्षिप्य निष्पिष्य विननाद च॥६॥
verses.english: O best of the Bharata race, having thus whirled him high for one hundred times, he (Bhima) pressed his knee against his (Jarasandha's) backbone and broke his body, into two parts. (Having thus killed him), he roared aloud.

verses.sanskrit: करे गृहीत्वा चरणं द्वेधा चक्रे महाबलः॥७॥
तस्य निष्पिष्यमाणस्य पाण्डवस्य च गर्जतः। अभवत्तुमुलो नादः सर्वप्राणिभयङ्करः॥८॥
verses.english: The roar of the Pandava (Bhima), mingled with that of Jarasandha while he was being broken by Bhima's knee, raised such a loud roar that it struck fear into the heart of every creature.

verses.sanskrit: वित्रेसुर्मागधाः सर्वे स्त्रीणां गर्भाश्च सुस्रुवुः। भीमसेनस्य नादेन जरासन्धस्य चैव ह॥९॥
verses.english: The people of Magadha becaine dumb with fear; and even many women were prematurely delivered by the roars of Bhima and Jarasandha.

verses.sanskrit: किं नु स्याद्धिमवान्भिन्नः किं नु स्विद्दीर्यते मही। इति वै मागधा जज्ञुर्भीमसेनस्य निःस्वनात्॥१०॥
verses.english: Hearing the roars of Bhima, the people of Magadha thought that either Himalayas were coming down or the earth is being rent asunder.

verses.sanskrit: ततो राज्ञः कुलद्वारि प्रसुप्तमिव तं नृपम्। रात्रौ गतासुमुत्सृज्य निश्चक्रमुररिन्दमाः॥११॥
verses.english: The chastiser of foes (Krishna) left at night the dead body of the king at the palace gate, as if he was but asleep. They then came out (of the palace).

verses.sanskrit: जरासन्धरथं कृष्णो योजयित्वा बान्धवान्। आरोप्य भ्रातरौ चैव मोक्षयामास बान्धवान्॥१२॥
verses.english: Krishna made ready the chariot of Jarasandha with the excellent standard and he then placed on it the two brothers (Bhima and Arjuna). He then liberated the friends (the captive kings).

verses.sanskrit: ते वै रत्नुभुजं कृष्णं रत्नार्हाः पृथिवीश्वराः। राजानश्चक्रुरासाद्य मोक्षिता महतो भयात्॥१३॥
verses.english: Having been freed from their great fear, those monarchs, those kings, those possessors came of gems came to Krishna and presented him with many gems and jewels.

verses.sanskrit: अक्षतः शस्त्रसंपन्नो जितारिः सह राजभिः। रथमास्थाय तं दिव्यं निर्जगाम गिरिव्रजात्॥१४॥
verses.english: Unwounded, (now) with (many) weapons, vanquishing the foe, he (Krishna), riding on the celestials car (of Jarasandha) came out with the kings from the city of Girivraja.

verses.sanskrit: यः स सोदर्यवान्नाम द्वियोधी कृष्णसारथिः। अभ्यासघाती संदृश्यो दुर्जयः सर्वराजभिः॥१५॥
verses.english: He, who wielded the bow with both hands, who was invincible to all kings, and who was exceedingly handsome and well skilled in killing the enemy, out with that possessors of great strength Bhima, and Krishna drove the car.

verses.sanskrit: भीमार्जुनाभ्यां योधाभ्यामास्थितः कृष्णसारथिः। शुशुभे रथवर्योऽसौ दुर्जयः सर्वधन्विभिः॥१६॥
verses.english: That celestials car, invincible to all warriors, ridden by the heroes, Bhima and Arjuna, and driven by Krishna, looked exceedingly beautiful.
verses.bhavadeepa: सोदर्यवान्‌ भीमयुक्तः द्वियोधी द्वाभ्यां हस्ताभ्यां शराणां प्रक्षेपात् अभ्यासघाती पुनःपुनरावृत्तिरभ्यासः तं परकीयं हन्तुं शीलमस्य धनुर्विद्यायां परोत्कर्षजेता । संदृश्यः रमणीयाङ्गः ॥१५॥

verses.sanskrit: शक्रविष्णू हि सङ्ग्रामे चेरतुस्तारकामये। रथेन तेन वै कृष्ण उपारुह्य ययौ तदा॥१७॥
verses.english: It was in this very car that Indra and Vishnu fought in the battle of old (with the Asuras) in which Taraka (the wife of Brihaspati) was cause, and the result of which was a great slaughter. Riding on that very car, Krishna now came out.

verses.sanskrit: तप्तचामीकराभेण किङ्किणीजालमालिना। मेघनिर्घोषनादेन जैत्रेणामित्रघातिना॥१८॥
verses.english: It possessed the splendour of heated gold, it was adorned with rows of jingling bells, it had wheels that made the clatter like the roars of the clouds, it was ever victorious in battle and it always killed the foes.
verses.bhavadeepa: शक्रविष्णू हिशब्द इवार्थे । तारकामये तारका तारा बृहस्पतिभार्या सैव आमयवत्‌ विनाशहेतुर्यस्मिन्‌ । आमयो रोगः ॥१७॥

verses.sanskrit: येन शक्रो दानवानां जघान नवतीर्नव। तं प्राप्य समहृष्यन्त रथं ते पुरुषर्थभाः॥१९॥
verses.english: Riding on it, Shakra (Indra) killed ninety nine Danavas of old. Those best of men (Krishna & c.) were exceedingly pleased on obtaining this car.

verses.sanskrit: ततः कृष्णं महाबाहुं भ्रातृभ्यां सहितं तदा। रथस्थं मागधा दृष्ट्वा समपद्यन्त विस्मिताः॥२०॥
verses.english: Seeing the long-armed Krishna on the chariot with the two brothers, (Bhima and Arjuna), the people of Magadha became very much astonished.

verses.sanskrit: हयैर्दिव्यैः समायुक्तो रथो वायुसमो जवे। अधिष्ठितः स शुशुभे कृष्णेनातीव भारत॥२१॥
verses.english: O descendant of Bharata, that car, with which were yoked celestials horses with the speed of the wind and which was driven by Krishna, looked exceedingly beautiful.

verses.sanskrit: असङ्गो देवविहितस्तस्मिन्रथवरे ध्वजः। योजनाद्ददृशे श्रीमानिन्द्रायुधसमप्रभः॥२२॥
verses.english: On this best of cars there was a flag-staff without being visibly attached thereto. It was the product of celestials art. That beautiful flat staff could be seen from a distance of a Yojana, and it had the splendour of the rainbow.

verses.sanskrit: चिन्तयामास कृष्णोऽथ गरुत्मन्तं स चाभ्ययात्। क्षणे तस्मिन्स तेनासीच्चैत्यवृक्ष इवोत्थितः॥२३॥
verses.english: When coming out, Krishna thought of Garuda. As soon as thought of, he came there like a large tree worshipped by all.

verses.sanskrit: व्यादितास्यैर्महानादैः सह भूतैर्ध्वजालयैः। तस्मिन्रथवरे तस्थौ गुरुत्मान्पन्नगाशनः॥२४॥
verses.english: The eater of snakes, Garuda of iminense weight of body, sat on that excellent car along with innumerable other open-mouthed and fearfully roaring creatures on its flag-staff.

verses.sanskrit: दुर्निरीक्ष्यो हि भूतानां तेजसाऽऽभ्यधिकं बभौ। आदित्य इव मध्याह्ने सहस्रकिरणावृतः॥२५॥
verses.english: Thereupon that best of cars be came more dazzling than before; and like the sun in midday, surrounded by thousand rays, it became incapable of being looked at by any living creature.

verses.sanskrit: न स सज्जति वृक्षेषु शस्त्रैश्चापि न रिष्यते। दिव्यो ध्वजवरो राजन्दृश्यते चेह मानुषैः॥२६॥
verses.english: O king, such was that celestialsly made and the best flagstaff that it never struck against a tree. The weapons could not any way injure it, although it was visible to the human eye.

verses.sanskrit: तमास्थाय रथं दिव्यं पर्जन्यसमनिः स्वनम्। निर्ययौ पुरुषव्याघ्रः पाण्डवाभ्यां सहाच्युतः॥२७॥
verses.english: That best of men, Achyuta (Krishna), riding with the two Pandava (Bhima and Arjuna) on that celestials car, the wheels of which made a clatter like the roars of the clouds, came out (of Girivraja).

verses.sanskrit: यं लेभे वासवाद्राजा वसुस्तस्माद्बृहद्रथः। बृहद्रथात्क्रमेणैव प्राप्तो बार्हद्रथं नृप॥२८॥
verses.english: It (the car) was obtained by the king Vasu from Vasava (Indra), From Vasu it was obtained by Brihadratha; from Brihadratha it was in due course obtained by the king (Jarasandha), the son of Brihadratha.

verses.sanskrit: स निर्याय महाबाहुः पुण्डरीकेक्षणस्ततः। गिरिव्रजाद्बहिस्तस्थौ समदेशे महायशाः॥२९॥
verses.english: The long armed, the lotus-eyed and the greatly famous (Krishna), coming out (of Girivraja), stopped on a level plain outside the city.

verses.sanskrit: तत्रैनं नागराः सर्वे सत्कारेणाभ्ययुस्तदा। ब्राह्मणप्रमुखा राजन्विधिदृष्टेन कर्मणा॥३०॥
verses.english: O king, all the citizens with the Brahmans at their head then hastened there to adore him according to the due rites of the ordinance.

verses.sanskrit: बन्धनाद्विप्रमुक्ताश्च राजानो मधुसूदनम्। पूजयामासुरूचुश्च स्तुतिपूर्वमिदं वचः॥३१॥
verses.english: The kings, who had been liberated from their confinement, worshipped the slayer of Madhu; and they thus spoke to him eulogistic words.

verses.sanskrit: नैतच्चित्रं महाबाहो त्वयि देवकिनन्दने। भीमार्जुनबलोपेते धर्मस्य प्रतिपालनम्॥३२॥
verses.english: O mighty armed (hero), O son of Devaki, such an act of virtue is not (at all) wonderful in you. Assisted as you are by the prowess of Bhima and Arjuna, you have to-day rescued the kings who sank in the fearful mire of sorrow in the lake of Jarasandha.

verses.sanskrit: जरासन्धह्रदे घोरे दुःखपङ्के निमज्जताम्। राज्ञां समभ्युद्धरणं यदिदं कृतमद्य वै॥३३॥
विष्णो समवसन्नानां गिरिदुर्गे सुदारुणे। दिष्ट्या मोक्षाद्यशो दीप्तमाप्तं ते यदुनन्दन॥३४॥
verses.english: O Vishnu, O descendant of Yadu, we were languishing in the fearful hill-fort (of Jaransandha); from our good fortune alone, you have rescued us and earned a great renown.

verses.sanskrit: किं कर्मः पुरुषव्याघ्र शाधि नः प्रणतिस्थितान्। कृतमित्येव तद्विद्धि नृपैर्यद्यपि दुष्करम्॥३५॥
verses.english: O best of men, we bow to you, command us what we shall do. However difficult it may be to carry out your command, know, it is already carried out by the kings (ourselves)”.

verses.sanskrit: तानुवाच हृषीकेशः समाश्वास्य महामनाः। युधिष्ठिरो राजसूयं क्रतुमार्हतुमिच्छति॥३६॥
verses.english: Giving them every assurance, thus replied to them Hrishikesha (Krishna), "Yudhishthira is desirous of performing the Rajasuya (sacrifice).

verses.sanskrit: तस्य धर्मप्रवृत्तस्य पार्थिवत्वं चिकीर्षतः। सर्वैर्भवद्भिर्विज्ञाय साहाय्यं क्रियतामिति॥३७॥
verses.english: That king, ever devoted to virtue, is solicitous to acquire the imperial dignity. Knowing this from me, help him in his attempt."

verses.sanskrit: ततः सुप्रीतमनसस्ते नृपा नृपसत्तम। तथेत्येवाब्रुवन्सर्वे प्रतिगृह्यास्य तां गिरम्॥३८॥
verses.english: O best of kings, thereupon all those monarchs, saying "Be it so, “accepted with joyous heart all that Krishna said.

verses.sanskrit: रत्नभाजं च दाशार्हं चक्रुस्ते पृथिवीश्वराः। कृच्छ्राज्जग्राह गोविन्दस्तेषां तदनुकम्पया॥३९॥
verses.english: The monarchs made presents of jewels to the hero of Dasarha race (Krishna). Govinda (Krishna), out of kindness towards them, only took a portion of those presents.

verses.sanskrit: जरासन्धात्मजश्चैव सहदेवो महामनाः। निर्ययौ सजनामात्यः पुरस्कृत्य पुरोहितम्॥४०॥
verses.english: The son of Jarasandha, the high-minded Sahadeva, came out there with his relatives and his ministers, his priest being at the head of the procession.

verses.sanskrit: स नीचैः प्रणतो भूत्वा बहुरत्नपुरोगमः। सहदेवो नृणां देवं वासुदेवमुपस्थितः॥४१॥
verses.english: Sahadeva bowed low before the god among men, Vasudeva; and presenting him many gems and jewels, he worshipped him.

verses.sanskrit: भयार्ताय ततस्तस्मै कृष्णो दत्त्वाऽभयं तदा। आददेस्य महार्हाणि रत्नानि पुरुषोत्तमः॥४२॥
verses.english: That best of men (Krishna) gave every assurance to that very much frightened prince and accepted his very valuable presents.

verses.sanskrit: अभ्यर्षिञ्चत तत्रैव जरासन्धात्मजं मुदा। गत्वैकत्वं च कृष्णेन पार्थाभ्यां चैव सत्कृतः॥४३॥
verses.english: He (Krishna) gladly installed there the son of Jarasandha; and thus being installed on the throne of Magadha by those exalted men and having been obtained the friendship of Krishna and being treated with respect and kindness by the two sons of Pritha, the mighty armed and the illustrious son of Jarasandha (Sahadeva) entered the city of the son of Brihadratha (Jarasandha).

verses.sanskrit: विवेश राजा द्युतिमान्बार्हद्रथपुरं नृप। अभिषिक्तो महाबाहुर्जारासन्धिर्महात्मभिः॥४४॥
कृष्णस्तु सह पार्थाभ्यां श्रिया परमया युतः। रत्नान्यादाय भूरीणि प्रययौ पुरुषर्षभः॥४५॥
verses.english: That best of men (Krishna), accompanied by the sons of Pritha and enriched with much wealth and laden with numerous jewels, went away (from Girivraja).

verses.sanskrit: इन्द्रप्रस्थमुपागम्य पाण्डवाभ्यां सहाच्युतः। समेत्य धर्मराजानं प्रीयमाणोऽभ्यभाषत॥४६॥
verses.english: Achyuta (Krishna), accompanied by the two Pandavas (Bhima and Arjuna), arrived at Indraprastha and went to Yudhishthira. He joyfully addressed the king and said,

verses.sanskrit: दिष्ट्या भीमेन बलवाञ्जरासन्धो निपातितः। राजानो मोक्षिताश्चैव बन्धनान्नृपसत्तम॥४७॥
verses.english: "O best of kings, the powerful Jarasandha has been killed by Bhima from good fortune. The kings, confined at Girivraja, have all been liberated.

verses.sanskrit: दिष्ट्या कुशलिनौ चेमौ भीमसेनधनञ्जयौ। पुनः स्वनगरं प्राप्तावक्षताविति भारत॥४८॥
verses.english: O descendant of Bharata, from good fortune, these two Bhima and Dhananjaya (Arjuna), are well. They have arrived at their own city unwounded”.

verses.sanskrit: ततो युधिष्ठिरः कृष्णं पूजयित्वा यथार्हतः। भीमसेनार्जुनौ चैव प्रहृष्टः परिषस्वजे॥४९॥
verses.english: Then Yudhishthira worshipped Krishna as he deserved; and he embrace Bhima and Arjuna in joy.

verses.sanskrit: ततः क्षीणे जरासन्धे भ्रातृभ्यां विहितं जयम्। अजातशत्रुरासाद्य मुमुदे भ्रातृभिः सह॥५०॥
verses.english: Having obtained victory through the agency of his brothers by the death of Jarasandha, Ajatashatru (Yudhishthira) passed his time with his brothers in great merriment.

verses.sanskrit: यथावयः समागम्य भ्रातृभिः सह पाण्डवः। सत्कृत्य पूजयित्वा च विससर्ज नराधिपान्॥५१॥
verses.english: The Pandava (Yudhishthira) with his brothers came to the kings (who had come to Indraprastha). Entertaining and worshipping them each according to his age, he sent them away.

verses.sanskrit: युधिष्ठिराभ्यनुज्ञातास्ते नृपा हृष्टमानसाः। जग्मुः स्वदेशांस्त्वरिता यानैरुच्चावचैस्ततः॥५२॥
verses.english: Having been commanded by Yudhishthira, those kings with joyful hearts and without any further loss of time started on their excellent vehicles for their own respective kingdoms.
verses.bhavadeepa: यथावयः ज्येष्ठानुक्रमेण प्रथमं भीमेन ततः कृष्णेन ततोऽर्जुनेन ॥५१॥

verses.sanskrit: एवं पुरुषशार्दूलो महाबुद्धिर्जनार्दनः। पाण्डवैर्घातयामास जरासन्धमरिं तदा॥५३॥
verses.english: O king, thus did that best of men, the greatly intelligent Janardana (Krishna) cause his foe Jarasandha to be killed through the instrumentality of the Pandavas.

verses.sanskrit: घातयित्वा जरासन्धं बुद्धिपूर्वमरिन्दमः। धर्मराजमनुज्ञाप्य पृथां कृष्णां च भारत॥५४॥
verses.english: O best of the Bharata race, when Krishna was about to start, the Pandavas with Yudhishthira at their head walked round that best of men (Krishna) who was never fatigued with exertion.

verses.sanskrit: ततो युधिष्ठिरमुखाः पाण्डवा भरतर्षभ। प्रदक्षिणमकुर्वन्त कृष्णमक्लिष्टकारिणम्॥५४॥
verses.english: O best of the Bharata race, when Krishna was about to start, the Pandavas with Yudhishthira at their head walked round that best of men (Krishna) who was never fatigued with exertion.

verses.sanskrit: सुभद्रां भीमसेनं च फाल्गुनं यमजौ तथा। धौम्यमामन्त्रयित्वा च प्रययौ स्वां पुरीं प्रति॥५५॥
verses.english: Subhadra, Bhimasena, Falguni (Arjuna), and the twins (Nakula and Sahadeva). Taking leave of Dhaumya, he started for his own city (Dwarka).

verses.sanskrit: ततो गते भगवति कृष्णे देवकिनन्दने। जयं लब्ध्वा सुविपुलं राज्ञां दत्त्वाऽभयं तदा॥५५॥
verses.english: Subhadra, Bhimasena, Falguni (Arjuna), and the twins (Nakula and Sahadeva). Taking leave of Dhaumya, he started for his own city (Dwarka).

verses.sanskrit: तेनैव रथमुख्येन मनसस्तुल्यगामिना। धर्मराजविसृष्टेन दिव्येनानादयन्दिशः॥५६॥
verses.english: On that celestialsly-made and the best of cars, which possessed the speed of mind, and which was given to him by Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira), and which filled the ten points of the horizon with the rattle of his wheels.

verses.sanskrit: संवर्धितं यशो भूयः कर्मणा तेन भारत। द्रौपद्याः पाण्डवा राजन्परां प्रीतिमवर्धयन्॥५९॥
verses.english: That feat of his increased the fame of the Pandavas. O descendant of Bharata, O king, the Pandavas (thus) increased the great happiness of Draupadi.

verses.sanskrit: तस्मिन्काले तु यद्युक्तं धर्मकामार्थसंहितम्। तद्राजा धर्मतश्चक्रे प्रजापालनकीर्तनम्॥६०॥
verses.english: Whatever is consistent with Dharma. Artha and Kama continued at that time to be properly performed by king Yudhishthira in the exercise of his duties in protecting his subjects.
